**Stephen Greg Hawkins** (born August 3, 1962) is an American [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") coach. He is currently an assistant men's basketball coach for [Southern Illinois University Carbondale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Illinois_University_Carbondale "Southern Illinois University Carbondale"), a position he has held since 2024. He had previously served as the head coach at [Western Michigan University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Michigan_University "Western Michigan University")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-wmubroncosbio-1) and [Quincy University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_University "Quincy University").

## Coaching career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steve_Hawkins&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Coaching career")]

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steve_Hawkins&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

Hawkins was born in [Ventura, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura,_California "Ventura, California"). Following his graduation from high school, Hawkins spent time as a high school basketball coach in the [Los Angeles area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_area "Los Angeles area") at [Villanova Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villanova_Preparatory_School "Villanova Preparatory School") and [St. Bonaventure High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Bonaventure_High_School "St. Bonaventure High School") during the early 1980s.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-wmubroncosbio-1) During this time he worked as an assistant at [UCLA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCLA "UCLA") basketball camps, serving as [chauffeur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauffeur "Chauffeur") for legendary Bruins coach [John Wooden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wooden "John Wooden"). While the two were stuck in traffic, they were able to talk basketball.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-mlive.com-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-3) Hawkins maintained the UCLA connection during his coaching career, often having Wooden speak to his teams at Quincy and Western Michigan.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-mlive.com-2) Former UCLA head coach [Larry Farmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Farmer_(basketball) "Larry Farmer (basketball)"), would later work for Hawkins as an assistant coach at Western Michigan from 2010–12 and again from 2013 until the present.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-4)

Hawkins later attended the [University of South Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Alabama "University of South Alabama"), graduating with a bachelor's degree in 1987. From 1984–87 he served as a student assistant to men's basketball head coach [Mike Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Hanks "Mike Hanks"). In 1989 he earned his [master's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree") in sports science from the [United States Sports Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Sports_Academy "United States Sports Academy").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-wmubroncosbio-1)

Hawkins served as an assistant coach at [Quincy University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_University "Quincy University") from 1987-1988 and 1990-1991 and [St. Andrews Presbyterian College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Andrews_Presbyterian_College "St. Andrews Presbyterian College") in 1989. He was promoted to head coach at Quincy in 1992 and served there for 9 seasons until joining the staff of [Robert McCullum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_McCullum "Robert McCullum") at Western Michigan in the spring of 2000.

### Western Michigan University

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steve_Hawkins&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Western Michigan University")]

Hawkins was named head coach at Western Michigan University on May 1, 2003, following the departure of head coach [Robert McCullum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_McCullum "Robert McCullum") to [South Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_South_Florida "University of South Florida").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-wmubroncosbio-1) Hawkins had served as an assistant coach on the WMU staff for the previous three seasons.

Under Hawkins, the Broncos have finished no worse than 3rd in the [Mid-American Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-American_Conference "Mid-American Conference") West Division. The team captured both the MAC regular season championship and [conference tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-American_Conference_men's_basketball_tournament "Mid-American Conference men's basketball tournament") championship in 2003–04. That squad eventually fell to [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanderbilt_University "Vanderbilt University") in the opening round of the [2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament").

Following the 2004–05 season, the Broncos participated in the [2005 National Invitation Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_National_Invitation_Tournament "2005 National Invitation Tournament").

In 2005 Hawkins was a finalist for the head coaching job at [DePaul University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DePaul_University "DePaul University") that eventually went to [Jerry Wainwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Wainwright "Jerry Wainwright").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-depaul-5) He has also received head coaching offers from the University of San Francisco (2004),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-depaul-5) the University of Nevada, and Southern Methodist University. He also received interest from Bradley University and Loyola-Chicago.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-6)

In July 2007, Hawkins was hospitalised for three days following a seizure in his office.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-7)

Following the 2007–08 basketball season, Hawkins was very critical of the post season basketball tournaments. Despite a 20-win season and a MAC West Division title, WMU was passed over for post season play, including the new [College Basketball Invitational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Basketball_Invitational "College Basketball Invitational").

Following the 2010–11 basketball season, Hawkins coached the Broncos in the [2011 CollegeInsider.com Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_CollegeInsider.com_Tournament "2011 CollegeInsider.com Tournament"). After a victory in the opening round against [Tennessee Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Tech "Tennessee Tech"), the Broncos fell in the second round to MAC rival [Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_at_Buffalo "University at Buffalo").

Following the 2012-13 basketballs season, Hawkins and Broncos participated in the [2013 College Basketball Invitational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_College_Basketball_Invitational "2013 College Basketball Invitational"). They won their first 2 games before falling to [George Mason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_George_Mason_Patriots_men's_basketball_team "2012–13 George Mason Patriots men's basketball team") in the semifinals.

The 2013-14 Broncos were one of the most successful of Hawkins' tenure, with a [Rainbow Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Western_Michigan_Broncos_men's_basketball_team#Rainbow_Classic "2013–14 Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball team") Championship, a MAC regular season championship, and a [MAC tournament championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_MAC_men's_basketball_tournament "2014 MAC men's basketball tournament"). The team made the NCAA tournament, where as a #14 seed they fell in the opening round to #3 seed [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2013–14 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team") by a score of 77-53. Following the season, Hawkins was named the 2014 MAC Men's Basketball Coach of the Year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-8)

On Wednesday, March 11, 2020, Western Michigan announced Hawkins would not return, ending his 17-year run as head coach.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-9)

### Quincy University (second stint)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steve_Hawkins&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Quincy University (second stint)")]

On March 9, 2022, Hawkins was hired as head coach of the [Quincy Hawks men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quincy_Hawks_men's_basketball "Quincy Hawks men's basketball") team.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-10) On April 15, 2024, Hawkins resigned as head coach to explore another opportunity.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-11)

### Southern Illinois University

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Steve_Hawkins&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Southern Illinois University")]

On April 15, 2024, Hawkins was hired as an assistant coach of the [Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Illinois_Salukis_men's_basketball "Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball") team under head coach [Scott Nagy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Nagy "Scott Nagy").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Hawkins#cite_note-12)

**Strange Boutique** is a band from [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") They were active between the years of 1987 and 1994 and released 4 full-length albums and 2 live albums on the [Bedazzled Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedazzled_Records "Bedazzled Records") label. They are also featured on several compilation albums. [Monica Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Richards "Monica Richards"), the lead singer of Strange Boutique, later went on to form the underground band [Faith and the Muse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_and_the_Muse "Faith and the Muse").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years, _Easter Island_ EP and _The Loved One_ (1987-1991)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years, Easter Island EP and The Loved One (1987-1991)")]

Monica Richards and drummer Daniel Ingram had formed the band **Madhouse** in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") in 1983, and throughout its four-year history, had transformed from punk-rock into a melodic mix, featuring the bass playing of Franz Kellner and the guitar work of Fred Smith, who joined the band in 1986 after leaving Beefeater.

In 1987, Madhouse sold their name to a jazz ensemble who was on a major label. Through a classified ad in the weekly DC City Paper, bassist Steve Willett joined the group; the chemistry was instant and within a short time an entirely new set of songs was written. As Strange Boutique, the band's material incorporated elements of the DC [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk") scene and melody. Developing a guitar-driven ethereal pop sound with world music influences, Strange Boutique was described as having "a swirling, soaring guitar, ethereal vocals, and a pulsating [rhythm section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_section "Rhythm section")."

Early recordings of “Step Softly” and “Feast Your Eyes” wound up on DC-based compilations and provided a calling card for the new lineup and sound. The band's first EP, _Easter Island_, featuring the pulsing lead track, “Quicksand Minds" followed in May of 1989. The new record and live shows received local attention. The performances featured a combination of Fred's guitar work, Monica's vocals, and the rhythm section of Danny and Steve.

Following a performance supporting [Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke") in D.C., the two bands struck an immediate friendship, and KJ gave Strange Boutique the support slot for their next UK shows. The band took the chance and flew to London, performing a number of well-received shows in support of Killing Joke.

In between live shows the band worked constantly on new material. Quickly leaving the early material behind, the group found its stride in yet another new batch of songs. The new stuff had a swagger and a groove... _the edges were soaked in reverb and Monica found a place on top of it all_. A limited 7” single featuring “A Happy Death” and a cover of [Magazine’s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine_(band) "Magazine (band)") “A Song From Under the Floorboards” was released on [Y&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y&T "Y&T") records.

Strange Boutique entered the studio in February, 1991 to record their long-awaited debut album _The Loved One_. The album, which featured a new recording of their EP favorite "Quicksand Minds", was released on their own Bedazzled Records in the Fall of 1991 Around this time, drummer Daniel Ingram left the band to explore his expanding musical interests. He joined England's [Swervedriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swervedriver "Swervedriver") for their 1992 world tour, and moved to London. Rand Blackwell joins the band as the new drummer.

### _Charm_, _The Kindest Worlds_ and breakup (1992-1994)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Charm, The Kindest Worlds and breakup (1992-1994)")]

The band recorded and released a new single, In A Heaven with a cover of David Bowie's "Heroes" on the B-side. The band performed extensively, touring the East Coast in support of the release.

In November 1992, Strange Boutique began recording their next record, again for their own Bedazzled Records. The second album, _Charm_, was released in February 1993. This album is considered the band's favorite; it finds SB in their most classic style.

The group traveled to the West Coast in March 1993 for a tour with This Ascension, as well as a show at [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco")'s House of Usher with [Switchblade Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switchblade_Symphony "Switchblade Symphony"). During this tour, the band performed for audiences in California and returned with an increased national fanbase.

1993, though, was a very difficult year for the band. All members experienced personal hardships, and the strain became all too apparent. Strange Boutique continued writing and touring in the ensuing months, but for numerous personal reasons, the band decided to go on a possibly permanent respite. The band entered the studio in November, 1993, one last time to record the last songs written, which became their third and final album, _The Kindest Worlds_, released in 1994.

When Strange Boutique said farewell in 1993, the band scattered across the country and found new creative outlets. Singer Monica Richards formed Faith and the Muse, guitarist Fred Smith landed in Blaxmyth and bassist Steve Willett joined DC guitar ensemble Tone. Drummer Rand Blackwell retreated to the mountains of [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina").

### First reunion and Collection release (2004)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First reunion and Collection release (2004)")]

On Saturday, July 3, 2004, Strange Boutique celebrated a brief reunion at The Black Cat in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_DC "Washington DC"). The band played with [This Ascension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Ascension "This Ascension") and [Siddal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siddal_(band)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Siddal (band) (page does not exist)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange_Boutique_(band)#cite_note-1) This one-off show coincided with the release of _Strange Boutique: The Collection - 1988-1994_, on [Metropolis Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_Records "Metropolis Records").

This event would be the last time they performed with Fred _"Freak"_ Smith on guitar.

### Fred Smith's death, reunion and band's revival (2017-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Fred Smith's death, reunion and band's revival (2017-present)")]

After the death of guitarist Fred _“Freak”_ Smith in 2017, singer Monica Richards and bassist Steve Willett began reminiscing about their love of Fred and the music they wrote with him. This began a dialogue about getting together in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_DC "Washington DC") for an evening of music.

In 2019, Strange Boutique reunited to begin practice for a single show in honor of Fred, yet something unexpected happened... While rehearsing with Dennis Kane who was filling in on guitar, it became apparent that even after such an extended hiatus, all the music of Strange Boutique came naturally to the new lineup. In June of that year, the club DC9 in Washington DC was the site of a Strange Boutique performance in celebration of Smith's life. Following the reception for the new lineup and the experience of [performing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance "Performance") together, the band decided to write new material.

Strange Boutique released their first new music in over 15 years, the _Jet Stream EP_. in 2021.

The band released a new single called "The Night Birds" on November 1st, 2024, from their upcoming fourth record, _Let the Lonely Heart Sing_, set to be released on June 10th, 2025. This marks their first full record after more than thirty years after their last album, _The Kindest Worlds_.

**Strange Boutique** is a band from [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") They were active between the years of 1987 and 1994 and released 4 full-length albums and 2 live albums on the [Bedazzled Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedazzled_Records "Bedazzled Records") label. They are also featured on several compilation albums. [Monica Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monica_Richards "Monica Richards"), the lead singer of Strange Boutique, later went on to form the underground band [Faith and the Muse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_and_the_Muse "Faith and the Muse").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early years, _Easter Island_ EP and _The Loved One_ (1987-1991)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years, Easter Island EP and The Loved One (1987-1991)")]

Monica Richards and drummer Daniel Ingram had formed the band **Madhouse** in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") in 1983, and throughout its four-year history, had transformed from punk-rock into a melodic mix, featuring the bass playing of Franz Kellner and the guitar work of Fred Smith, who joined the band in 1986 after leaving Beefeater.

In 1987, Madhouse sold their name to a jazz ensemble who was on a major label. Through a classified ad in the weekly DC City Paper, bassist Steve Willett joined the group; the chemistry was instant and within a short time an entirely new set of songs was written. As Strange Boutique, the band's material incorporated elements of the DC [post-punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-punk "Post-punk") scene and melody. Developing a guitar-driven ethereal pop sound with world music influences, Strange Boutique was described as having "a swirling, soaring guitar, ethereal vocals, and a pulsating [rhythm section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_section "Rhythm section")."

Early recordings of “Step Softly” and “Feast Your Eyes” wound up on DC-based compilations and provided a calling card for the new lineup and sound. The band's first EP, _Easter Island_, featuring the pulsing lead track, “Quicksand Minds" followed in May of 1989. The new record and live shows received local attention. The performances featured a combination of Fred's guitar work, Monica's vocals, and the rhythm section of Danny and Steve.

Following a performance supporting [Killing Joke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_Joke "Killing Joke") in D.C., the two bands struck an immediate friendship, and KJ gave Strange Boutique the support slot for their next UK shows. The band took the chance and flew to London, performing a number of well-received shows in support of Killing Joke.

In between live shows the band worked constantly on new material. Quickly leaving the early material behind, the group found its stride in yet another new batch of songs. The new stuff had a swagger and a groove... _the edges were soaked in reverb and Monica found a place on top of it all_. A limited 7” single featuring “A Happy Death” and a cover of [Magazine’s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine_(band) "Magazine (band)") “A Song From Under the Floorboards” was released on [Y&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y&T "Y&T") records.

Strange Boutique entered the studio in February, 1991 to record their long-awaited debut album _The Loved One_. The album, which featured a new recording of their EP favorite "Quicksand Minds", was released on their own Bedazzled Records in the Fall of 1991 Around this time, drummer Daniel Ingram left the band to explore his expanding musical interests. He joined England's [Swervedriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swervedriver "Swervedriver") for their 1992 world tour, and moved to London. Rand Blackwell joins the band as the new drummer.

### _Charm_, _The Kindest Worlds_ and breakup (1992-1994)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Charm, The Kindest Worlds and breakup (1992-1994)")]

The band recorded and released a new single, In A Heaven with a cover of David Bowie's "Heroes" on the B-side. The band performed extensively, touring the East Coast in support of the release.

In November 1992, Strange Boutique began recording their next record, again for their own Bedazzled Records. The second album, _Charm_, was released in February 1993. This album is considered the band's favorite; it finds SB in their most classic style.

The group traveled to the West Coast in March 1993 for a tour with This Ascension, as well as a show at [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco")'s House of Usher with [Switchblade Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switchblade_Symphony "Switchblade Symphony"). During this tour, the band performed for audiences in California and returned with an increased national fanbase.

1993, though, was a very difficult year for the band. All members experienced personal hardships, and the strain became all too apparent. Strange Boutique continued writing and touring in the ensuing months, but for numerous personal reasons, the band decided to go on a possibly permanent respite. The band entered the studio in November, 1993, one last time to record the last songs written, which became their third and final album, _The Kindest Worlds_, released in 1994.

When Strange Boutique said farewell in 1993, the band scattered across the country and found new creative outlets. Singer Monica Richards formed Faith and the Muse, guitarist Fred Smith landed in Blaxmyth and bassist Steve Willett joined DC guitar ensemble Tone. Drummer Rand Blackwell retreated to the mountains of [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina").

### First reunion and Collection release (2004)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First reunion and Collection release (2004)")]

On Saturday, July 3, 2004, Strange Boutique celebrated a brief reunion at The Black Cat in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_DC "Washington DC"). The band played with [This Ascension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Ascension "This Ascension") and [Siddal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siddal_(band)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Siddal (band) (page does not exist)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strange_Boutique_(band)#cite_note-1) This one-off show coincided with the release of _Strange Boutique: The Collection - 1988-1994_, on [Metropolis Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolis_Records "Metropolis Records").

This event would be the last time they performed with Fred _"Freak"_ Smith on guitar.

### Fred Smith's death, reunion and band's revival (2017-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Strange_Boutique_(band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Fred Smith's death, reunion and band's revival (2017-present)")]

After the death of guitarist Fred _“Freak”_ Smith in 2017, singer Monica Richards and bassist Steve Willett began reminiscing about their love of Fred and the music they wrote with him. This began a dialogue about getting together in [Washington DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_DC "Washington DC") for an evening of music.

In 2019, Strange Boutique reunited to begin practice for a single show in honor of Fred, yet something unexpected happened... While rehearsing with Dennis Kane who was filling in on guitar, it became apparent that even after such an extended hiatus, all the music of Strange Boutique came naturally to the new lineup. In June of that year, the club DC9 in Washington DC was the site of a Strange Boutique performance in celebration of Smith's life. Following the reception for the new lineup and the experience of [performing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance "Performance") together, the band decided to write new material.

Strange Boutique released their first new music in over 15 years, the _Jet Stream EP_. in 2021.

The band released a new single called "The Night Birds" on November 1st, 2024, from their upcoming fourth record, _Let the Lonely Heart Sing_, set to be released on June 10th, 2025. This marks their first full record after more than thirty years after their last album, _The Kindest Worlds_.

**Christine Ellen Hynde** (born September 7, 1951) is an [American-British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-British "American-British")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-LADN-2) singer, songwriter, and musician. She is a founding member of the rock band [the Pretenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pretenders "The Pretenders") and is the band's lead vocalist, guitarist, and primary songwriter. Hynde is the band's only original member and is the only continuous member of the Pretenders, having appeared on every studio album released by the band.

Hynde formed the Pretenders in [Hereford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereford "Hereford"), England, in 1978, with [Pete Farndon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Farndon "Pete Farndon"), [James Honeyman-Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Honeyman-Scott "James Honeyman-Scott"), and [Martin Chambers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Chambers "Martin Chambers").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-spin/1986-12/hynde-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-bbc/hereford/musicmap/pretenders-4) She has also recorded a number of songs with other musicians, including [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra"), [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher"), and [UB40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UB40 "UB40"). Hynde recorded her first solo album, _[Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm\_(Chrissie\_Hynde\_album) "Stockholm (Chrissie Hynde album)")_, in 2014. She was inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") in 2005 as a member of the Pretenders.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Hynde was born in [Akron, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akron,_Ohio "Akron, Ohio"), United States, the daughter of a part-time secretary and a [Yellow Pages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_Pages "Yellow Pages") manager,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-:0-5) and grew up in nearby [Cuyahoga Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuyahoga_Falls,_Ohio "Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-6) She graduated from [Firestone High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firestone_High_School "Firestone High School") in Akron but stated: "I was never too interested in high school. I mean, I never went to a dance, I never went out on a date, I never went steady. It became pretty awful for me. Except, of course, I could go see bands, and that was the kick. I used to go to [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") just to see any band. So I was in love a lot of the time, but mostly with guys in bands that I had never met. For me, knowing that [Brian Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Jones "Brian Jones") was out there, and later that [Iggy Pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iggy_Pop "Iggy Pop") was out there, made it kind of hard for me to get too interested in the guys that were around me. I had, uh, bigger things in mind."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-7)

## Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career")]

Hynde became interested in [hippie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippie "Hippie")[counterculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterculture "Counterculture"), [Eastern mysticism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_mysticism "Eastern mysticism"), and vegetarianism.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-8) While attending [Kent State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_State_University "Kent State University")'s Art School for three years, she joined Sat. Sun. Mat., a band which included [Mark Mothersbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Mothersbaugh "Mark Mothersbaugh"), later of [Devo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devo "Devo").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) Hynde was also caught up in the [Kent State massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kent_State_massacre "Kent State massacre") on May 4, 1970, in which the boyfriend of one of her friends was among the four victims.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Reckless-10)

In May 1973, Hynde moved to London.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-cnn/travel/chrissie-hynde-11) With her art background, she got a job in an architectural firm but left after eight months. It was then that she met rock journalist [Nick Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Kent "Nick Kent") and landed a position at the music magazine _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ (_New Musical Express_),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-12) writing what she subsequently described as "half-baked philosophical drivel and nonsensical tirades."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-13) Afterwards Hynde got a job at [Malcolm McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_McLaren "Malcolm McLaren") and [Vivienne Westwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivienne_Westwood "Vivienne Westwood")'s clothing store, [Sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_(boutique) "Sex (boutique)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-14) Hynde attempted to start a band in France, before her return to Cleveland in 1975,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-:0-5) and joined a rhythm and blues group, Jack Rabbit.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-15)

After living in Tucson,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) she returned to France in 1975 at the invitation of Michael Fradji Memmi, bass player of _[the Frenchies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Frenchies?action=edit&redlink=1 "The Frenchies (page does not exist)")_ ([fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/The%20Frenchies "fr:The Frenchies")), which she joined as the singer.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) She returned to London in 1976 in the midst of the early [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") movement. At one point she tried to convince [Steve Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jones_(musician) "Steve Jones (musician)") and then [Johnny Rotten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Rotten "Johnny Rotten") (of [the Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sex_Pistols "The Sex Pistols"), who were managed by McLaren), to [marry her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage_of_convenience "Marriage of convenience") to get her a work permit.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-17) Hynde's version of this episode has it that Rotten "offered to go to a registry office with me and do the unmentionable," but when he subsequently withdrew, [Sid Vicious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Vicious "Sid Vicious") volunteered to take his place.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Vicious_%22marriage%22-18) Upon arrival at the registry office the following morning, they found it "closed for an extended holiday" and were unable to attend the following day due to Vicious making a court appearance.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Vicious_%22marriage%22-18) In late 1976, Hynde responded to an advertisement in _[Melody Maker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melody\_Maker "Melody Maker")_ for band members and attended an audition for the band that would become [999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/999_(band) "999 (band)"). [Jon Moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Moss "Jon Moss") (who would later be in [Culture Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_Club "Culture Club")) and [Tony James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_James_(musician) "Tony James (musician)") of [Generation X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generation_X_(band) "Generation X (band)") also auditioned.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-19) Later, Hynde tried to start a group with [Mick Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jones_(The_Clash) "Mick Jones (The Clash)") from [the Clash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Clash "The Clash").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9)

After the lack of success with the band, Malcolm McLaren placed her as a guitarist in [Masters of the Backside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_of_the_Backside "Masters of the Backside") but she was asked to leave the group just as it became [the Damned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Damned_(band) "The Damned (band)").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) After a brief spell in the band [Johnny Moped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Moped "Johnny Moped"), Mick Jones invited Hynde to join his band on their initial tour of Britain.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) Hynde recollected of that period,

> It was great, but my heart was breaking. I wanted to be in a band so bad. And to go to all the gigs, to see it so close up, to be living in it and not to have a band was devastating to me. When I left, I said, "Thanks a lot for lettin' me come along," and I went back and went weeping on the Underground throughout London. All the people I knew in town, they were all in bands. And there I was, like the real loser, you know? Really the loser.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-stone-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-21)

Hynde also spent a short time with punk band [the Moors Murderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Moors_Murderers_(band) "The Moors Murderers (band)") in 1978. Named after [a pair of child-killers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Moors_Murderers "The Moors Murderers"), the band consisted of future [Visage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visage_(band) "Visage (band)") front man [Steve Strange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Strange "Steve Strange") on vocals, Vince Ely on drums, with [Mark Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ryan_(guitarist) "Mark Ryan (guitarist)") (a.k.a. the Kid), and Hynde on guitar. The band's name alone was enough to start controversy, and she soon distanced herself from the group. As noted in _NME,_ Hynde said: "I'm not in the group, I only rehearsed with them." She stated: "Steve Strange and [Soo Catwoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soo_Catwoman "Soo Catwoman") had the idea for the group, and asked me to help them out on guitar, which I did, even though I was getting my own group together and still am."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-22)

## The Pretenders

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: The Pretenders")]

Main article: [The Pretenders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pretenders "The Pretenders")

In 1978, Hynde made a demo tape and gave it to Dave Hill, owner of the Real Records label.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-23) Hill stepped in to manage her career, and began by paying off the back rent owed on her rehearsal room in [Covent Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covent_Garden "Covent Garden"), London.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Reckless-10) Hill also advised Hynde to take her time and get a band together. In the spring of 1978, Hynde met bass guitarist [Pete Farndon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Farndon "Pete Farndon") and they selected a band consisting of [James Honeyman-Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Honeyman-Scott "James Honeyman-Scott") (guitar, vocals, keyboards) and [Martin Chambers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Chambers "Martin Chambers") (drums, vocals, percussion).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) The name "the Pretenders" was inspired by the [Sam Cooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Cooke "Sam Cooke") version of [the Platters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Platters "The Platters")' 1955 R&B hit song "[The Great Pretender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_Pretender "The Great Pretender")."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-24)

They recorded a demo tape (including "Precious", "The Wait," and a [Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinks "The Kinks") cover, "[Stop Your Sobbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_Your_Sobbing "Stop Your Sobbing")"), handed it to Hynde's friend [Nick Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Lowe "Nick Lowe"), produced a single ("Stop Your Sobbing"/"The Wait"), and performed their first gig at a club in Paris. The single was released in January 1979 and hit no. 33 in the UK. A second single "Kid" followed to similar success in July 1979. In November 1979, the Pretenders released their first signature single "[Brass in Pocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass_in_Pocket "Brass in Pocket")" in the UK, which hit UK number 1 on January 19, 1980, the same date as their [eponymous first album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretenders_(album) "Pretenders (album)").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-25) Both went on to similar chart success worldwide.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Pretenders_Dec_81.JPG/250px-Pretenders_Dec_81.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pretenders_Dec_81.JPG)

The Pretenders playing at London's [Dominion Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_Theatre "Dominion Theatre") in 1981

The band released an [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") album, _[Extended Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended\_Play\_(Pretenders\_EP) "Extended Play (Pretenders EP)")_, on March 30, 1981; they released _[Pretenders II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretenders\_II "Pretenders II")_ later in the summer. "[Talk of the Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_of_the_Town_(Pretenders_song) "Talk of the Town (Pretenders song)")" and "Message of Love" were on both. The Pretenders lineup changed repeatedly over the next decade. Honeyman-Scott died of a drug overdose on June 16, 1982, just days after Farndon had been fired from the band. Farndon also died of a drug overdose the following year.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) After re-forming with a caretaker lineup (Martin Chambers, Billy Bremner, Tony Butler, and Jeremy Allom) for their next single, "[Back on the Chain Gang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_on_the_Chain_Gang "Back on the Chain Gang")", the band settled down with [Robbie McIntosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robbie_McIntosh "Robbie McIntosh") (guitar) and [Malcolm Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Foster "Malcolm Foster") (bass) during the recording of their next album, the worldwide hit _[Learning to Crawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning\_to\_Crawl "Learning to Crawl")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) Chambers left the band in the mid-1980s before the _[Get Close](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get\_Close "Get Close")_ album was released in 1986.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) The album included the hits "[Don't Get Me Wrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Get_Me_Wrong "Don't Get Me Wrong")" and "[My Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Baby_(Pretenders_song) "My Baby (Pretenders song)")."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-27) Amidst the ever-changing lineup, Hynde endured as the sole original Pretender until Chambers' return in the mid-1990s. Hynde was the only stable member of the band during this period.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-28) In 1994, the band had another hit, the ballad "[I'll Stand by You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Stand_by_You "I'll Stand by You")."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-The_Great_Rock_Discography-29)

Hynde continued with the Pretenders into the new century, both in new recording as well as multiple tours worldwide. New Pretenders albums emerged in 2002 (_[Loose Screw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loose\_Screw "Loose Screw")_), 2008 (_[Break Up the Concrete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break\_Up\_the\_Concrete "Break Up the Concrete")_,) and 2016 (_[Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alone\_(The\_Pretenders\_album) "Alone (The Pretenders album)")_).

Hynde was inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") in 2005 as a member of the Pretenders.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-30) The ceremony was held at the [Waldorf-Astoria Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waldorf-Astoria_Hotel "Waldorf-Astoria Hotel") in Manhattan, New York City.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-31)

In 2016, the band collaborated with [Dan Auerbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Auerbach "Dan Auerbach") of [the Black Keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Keys "The Black Keys") on the album _Alone_. This album was released as a Pretenders' album, though Hynde was the only original member to appear on it.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-32) The new band also played a concert for the BBC at the Maida Vale studio.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-33) In 2016, Hynde and the Pretenders opened for [Stevie Nicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Nicks "Stevie Nicks").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-34)

In July 2020, the Pretenders released their 11th studio album _[Hate for Sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hate\_for\_Sale "Hate for Sale")_. The album was well received critically and obtained a score of 78 on the critical aggregator Metacritic.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-35)

On March 9, 2022, Hynde performed a rendition of the Pretenders song "[I'll Stand By You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'll_Stand_By_You "I'll Stand By You")" at Night for Ukraine, a fundraising benefit held at the [Roundhouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundhouse_(venue) "Roundhouse (venue)") in north London. Funds raised were donated to the [Disasters Emergency Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disasters_Emergency_Committee "Disasters Emergency Committee") appeal, to provide aid to people fleeing Ukraine following the [Russian invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine"). The event was organized by [Fabien Riggall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabien_Riggall "Fabien Riggall") in collaboration with the Ukrainian pop duo [Bloom Twins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_Twins "Bloom Twins").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-36)

On June 24, 2023, Hynde and the band played the [Glastonbury Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glastonbury_Festival_2023 "Glastonbury Festival 2023") with guest artist [Johnny Marr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Marr "Johnny Marr"). [Dave Grohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Grohl "Dave Grohl") also guested on drums for one song.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-38)

## Other musical projects

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Other musical projects")]

Hynde, along with [Curved Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curved_Air "Curved Air")'s [Sonja Kristina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonja_Kristina "Sonja Kristina"), sang backing vocals on [Mick Farren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Farren "Mick Farren")'s 1978 album _[Vampires Stole My Lunch Money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vampires\_Stole\_My\_Lunch\_Money "Vampires Stole My Lunch Money")_ and also on _Hurt_ by [Chris Spedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Spedding "Chris Spedding"). She also sang backing on a track, "Nite Klub", on [the Specials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Specials "The Specials")' [eponymous debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Specials_(album) "The Specials (album)").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-39) Hynde sang a duet with [INXS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INXS "INXS") on their album _[Full Moon, Dirty Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full\_Moon,\_Dirty\_Hearts "Full Moon, Dirty Hearts")_ in 1993. She appears on the title track of the album.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-40) Hynde sang the vocals on the track "[State of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Independence "State of Independence") Part II" on a [Moodswings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moodswings_(band) "Moodswings (band)") album named _[Moodfood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moodfood "Moodfood")_, which was played during the closing credits on the soundtrack of _[Single White Female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single\_White\_Female "Single White Female")_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-41) She provided backing vocals on Morrissey's single "My Love Life" in 1991 and again on b-side "Shame Is The Name" in 2009.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-42)

Hynde recorded a duet with [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") on his 1994 album _[Duets II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duets\_II\_(Frank\_Sinatra\_album) "Duets II (Frank Sinatra album)")_. They performed the song "[Luck Be a Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luck_Be_a_Lady "Luck Be a Lady")." In 1995, Hynde made an acting appearance as fictional character Stephanie Schiffer on the US television comedy _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_. She was in the episode "The One with the Baby on the Bus", in which she performed "[Angel of the Morning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel_of_the_Morning "Angel of the Morning")" and the comedy song "[Smelly Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smelly_Cat "Smelly Cat")" (which she co-wrote) with [Lisa Kudrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Kudrow "Lisa Kudrow") as [Phoebe Buffay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoebe_Buffay "Phoebe Buffay") on acoustic guitar.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-43) Also in 1995, Hynde sang a cover of "[Love Can Build a Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Can_Build_a_Bridge "Love Can Build a Bridge")" with [Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher "Cher") and [Neneh Cherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neneh_Cherry "Neneh Cherry").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-44)[Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton") appeared on the track, supplying the lead guitar solo that is featured in the song's instrumental bridge.

In 1997, the [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI "EMI") publishing company issued a cease and desist request to [Rush Limbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rush_Limbaugh "Rush Limbaugh"), who for years had been using an edited instrumental version of Hynde's song "[My City Was Gone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_City_Was_Gone "My City Was Gone")" for the broadcast's opening theme. When the request came to Hynde's attention during a radio interview, she said her parents loved and listened to Rush and she did not mind its use. They agreed to a royalty contract which she retained and at one time used for a payment to PETA to raise awareness of chemical testing on animals.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-rs_rushlimbaugh-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-46)

Hynde's most popular non-Pretenders collaboration with another artist, chartwise, was her 1985 work with [UB40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UB40 "UB40") on a cover of [Sonny and Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonny_and_Cher "Sonny and Cher")'s "[I Got You Babe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Got_You_Babe "I Got You Babe")." The track topped the UK singles chart[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-47) and went as high as No.28 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in the U.S.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-48)

Hynde in 2007

On April 10, 1999, Hynde led the memorial concert "Here, There and Everywhere – A Concert for Linda" for her late close friend [Linda McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_McCartney "Linda McCartney") at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall"), London. Proceeds went to animal rights charities.

In 1999, Hynde played guitar and sang vocals with [Sheryl Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheryl_Crow "Sheryl Crow") on the song "[If It Makes You Happy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_It_Makes_You_Happy "If It Makes You Happy")" during a concert in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"). Hynde is mentioned prominently in the lyrics of the [Terence Trent D'Arby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Trent_D'Arby "Terence Trent D'Arby") song "Penelope Please."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-49) In 1998, Hynde sang a duet with her friend [Emmylou Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmylou_Harris "Emmylou Harris"), "She", accompanied by the Pretenders on the [Gram Parsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram_Parsons "Gram Parsons") tribute album, _[Return of the Grievous Angel: A Tribute to Gram Parsons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_the\_Grievous\_Angel:\_A\_Tribute\_to\_Gram\_Parsons "Return of the Grievous Angel: A Tribute to Gram Parsons")_. Hynde had previously reviewed Gram and Emmylou's debut country rock classic, _GP_. The version merges Emmylou's country rock and Hynde's reggae-tinged new wave. Hynde also recorded a song called "Cry (If You Don't Mind)" with the Spanish band [Jarabe de Palo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarabe_de_Palo "Jarabe de Palo") for their album _Un metro cuadrado – 1m²_.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-50) She supplied the voice for Siri, the clouded leopard in the movie _[Rugrats Go Wild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugrats\_Go\_Wild "Rugrats Go Wild")_ (2003) in which she sang a duet with [Bruce Willis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Willis "Bruce Willis").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-51)

In 2004, Hynde moved to [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), Brazil, for a couple of months in order to play with Brazilian musician [Moreno Veloso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moreno_Veloso "Moreno Veloso").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-52) She was also the vocalist on [Tube & Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tube_&_Berger "Tube & Berger")'s 2004 No.1 [Hot Dance Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Dance_Airplay "Hot Dance Airplay") track "[Straight Ahead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straight_Ahead_(Tube_&_Berger_song) "Straight Ahead (Tube & Berger song)")."[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-53) The track gave Hynde a No.1 track on the _Billboard_ charts.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-54) Likewise in 2005, Hynde duetted with [Ringo Starr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ringo_Starr "Ringo Starr") on a song entitled "Don't Hang Up," which can be heard on Starr's album _[Choose Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choose\_Love\_(album) "Choose Love (album)")_.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-55) Also in 2005, she collaborated with [Incubus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incubus_(band) "Incubus (band)") on a song called "Neither Of Us Can See." The song is on the soundtrack album for _[Stealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stealth\_(movie) "Stealth (movie)")_.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-56)

On October 17, 2008, she was an opening act for fellow Akron-area musicians [Devo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devo "Devo") at a special benefit concert at the Akron Civic Theater for then-presidential candidate [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"). [The Black Keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Black_Keys "The Black Keys"), another Akron-based band, and the then up-and-coming solo artist, Rachel Roberts, performed prior to her.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-57)

Hynde features as guest vocalist on [Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies")' 2009 Christmas single "Postcard From London"[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-58) and [Morrissey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morrissey "Morrissey")'s _[Years of Refusal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Years\_of\_Refusal "Years of Refusal")_ the same year.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-59)

Hynde and Welsh singer J.P. Jones formed a band called "J.P., Chrissie and the Fairground Boys", releasing an album, _Fidelity_, on August 24, 2010.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-60) Several stops on the tour were recorded and sold on USB [flash drives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_drives "Flash drives").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-61)

On February 5, 2011, Hynde and the Pretenders performed live on _[CMT Crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMT\_Crossroads "CMT Crossroads")_ with [Faith Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faith_Hill "Faith Hill") and her band, including songs from both catalogs.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-62)

Along with [John Cale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cale "John Cale") and [Nick Cave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Cave "Nick Cave"), Hynde played on [BBC Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Four "BBC Four") for the _Songwriter's Circle_ program on July 9, 1999. The concert took place at the Subterania Club in London, England and was released on DVD.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-63) She also later joined Cave in 2010 for a rendition of [Screamin' Jay Hawkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screamin'_Jay_Hawkins "Screamin' Jay Hawkins")' song "[I Put a Spell on You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Put_a_Spell_on_You "I Put a Spell on You")" as a benefit for the Haiti disasters. The song and music video featured performances by Mick Jones, [Glen Matlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Matlock "Glen Matlock"), [Shane MacGowan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_MacGowan "Shane MacGowan"), and [Bobby Gillespie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Gillespie "Bobby Gillespie") among others.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-64)

Hynde released a new album, _[Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm\_(Chrissie\_Hynde\_album) "Stockholm (Chrissie Hynde album)")_, on June 10, 2014. The album featured contributions from [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young") and [John McEnroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McEnroe "John McEnroe").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-65)

Hynde released _[Valve Bone Woe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valve\_Bone\_Woe "Valve Bone Woe")_, a jazz/pop album of selected covers with the Valve Bone Woe ensemble on September 6, 2019, produced by [Marius de Vries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marius_de_Vries "Marius de Vries").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-66) The album debuted at no. 32 on the Official UK album charts and at no. 1 on the UK Jazz and Blues chart.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-67)

Hynde and [James Walbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Walbourne "James Walbourne") were inspired by the surprise release of [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan")'s songs "[Murder Most Foul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_Most_Foul_(song) "Murder Most Foul (song)")" and "[I Contain Multitudes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Contain_Multitudes "I Contain Multitudes")" during the early part of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") to record nine of her favorite Dylan compositions, released initially via YouTube and subsequently on the 2021 album _Standing in the Doorway: Chrissie Hynde Sings Bob Dylan_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-rs_dylan-68)

A 2023 conversation with [Jörn Weisbrodt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B6rn_Weisbrodt "Jörn Weisbrodt") led Hynde to duet with Weisbrodt's husband [Rufus Wainwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Wainwright "Rufus Wainwright") on "[Always on My Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Always_on_My_Mind "Always on My Mind")", which became part of her 2025 _Duets Special_ album which also features [Brandon Flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Flowers "Brandon Flowers"), [Dave Gahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Gahan "Dave Gahan") and [Debbie Harry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Harry "Debbie Harry").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-rs_duets-69)

## Artistry and influence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Artistry and influence")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/ChrisHyndeROH290721_%2812_of_12%29.jpg/250px-ChrisHyndeROH290721_%2812_of_12%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ChrisHyndeROH290721_(12_of_12).jpg)

Chrissie Hynde performing in 2021 at the [Royal Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Opera_House "Royal Opera House")

Hynde has a [contralto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contralto "Contralto") vocal range.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-70) Until 1978, shortly before the advent of the Pretenders, Hynde had little idea what she sounded like.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Reckless_on_voice'-71) Hynde eschews formal voice training; she contends that "distinctive voices in rock are trained through years of many things: frustration, fear, loneliness, anger, insecurity, arrogance, narcissism, or just sheer perseverance – anything but a teacher."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Reckless_on_voice'-71)

In a 1994 interview, [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna_(entertainer) "Madonna (entertainer)") recalled of Hynde:

> "I saw her play in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park") [in August 1980, performing with the Pretenders]. She was amazing: the only woman I'd seen in performance where I thought, yeah, she's got balls, she's awesome! ... It gave me courage, inspiration, to see a woman with that kind of confidence in a man's world."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-72)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Hynde, born in the United States, has long maintained dual citizenship with the UK.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-LADN-2) In the 1970s, she went back to the US briefly before returning to the UK.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-culturecalling/2017/interview-hynde-73)

In 1980, Hynde met [Ray Davies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Davies "Ray Davies") (of [The Kinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kinks "The Kinks"), of whom Hynde had always been a fan) in a New York nightclub and the two began a relationship.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-louder-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-AllMusic-75) In 1979, The Pretenders' first single had been a cover of The Kinks' "[Stop Your Sobbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stop_Your_Sobbing "Stop Your Sobbing")", which Davies wrote. The Pretenders went on to cover another of Davies's songs, "[I Go to Sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Go_to_Sleep "I Go to Sleep")", which became a UK Top 10 hit for them in 1981. In 1982, Hynde and Davies planned to wed in [Guildford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guildford "Guildford"), but "the guy in the [register office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Register_office_(United_Kingdom) "Register office (United Kingdom)") took one look at us and suggested we come back another time."[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-getsurrey/10139985-76) The couple never did actually marry, but had a daughter together, Natalie, in 1983.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-personal_lewiston1997-77)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) After her relationship with Davies ended, Hynde married [Jim Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Kerr "Jim Kerr"), lead singer of the band [Simple Minds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_Minds "Simple Minds"), in 1984. Together they had a daughter, Yasmin, in 1985.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-guardian-9) They lived in [South Queensferry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Queensferry "South Queensferry") as well as [Kilmacolm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilmacolm "Kilmacolm"), Scotland[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-personal_lewiston1997-77) and divorced in 1990;[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-personal_lewiston1997-77) Hynde was married to Colombian artist and sculptor Lucho Brieva from 1997 to 2002.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-thefreelibrary/a061077299-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-cpd-79)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-personal_lewiston1997-77)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-80)

Hynde follows [Vaishnavism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnavism "Vaishnavism"), a branch of [Hinduism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinduism "Hinduism"), and travels to India once every year to further her studies.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-81)

Hynde lives in London[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-cnn/travel/chrissie-hynde-11) and has an apartment in the Northside Lofts in her hometown of Akron.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-82)

Hynde became a vegetarian in 1969 at the age of 18.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-84) She has described becoming a vegetarian as "the best thing that ever happened to me."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Being_vegetarian-85) She says that she came to regard meat-eaters with "distaste, almost contempt" but has learned to "live and associate with [them] but never respected them."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Being_vegetarian-85) Hynde is also an [animal rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_rights "Animal rights") activist and a supporter of [PETA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals")[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-86)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] and the animal rights group [Viva!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viva!_(organisation) "Viva! (organisation)").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-87)

Hynde has publicly campaigned against the extradition of [Julian Assange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Assange "Julian Assange") to the United States, and in February 2020 called on then President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") to "set him free."[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-88)

### Autobiography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Autobiography")]

Hynde published an autobiography, _[Reckless: My Life as a Pretender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reckless:\_My\_Life\_as\_a\_Pretender "Reckless: My Life as a Pretender")_, on September 8, 2015.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-Being_vegetarian-85)

In October 2018, Hynde released a limited edition book of her artworks, titled _Adding the Blue_, the name being taken from the final track on her 2014 solo album, _Stockholm_.

### Restaurant venture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Chrissie_Hynde&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Restaurant venture")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/2008-07-23_20-36-31vegiterranean.JPG/250px-2008-07-23_20-36-31vegiterranean.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2008-07-23_20-36-31vegiterranean.JPG)

The VegiTerranean restaurant and bar and bakery at Northside Lofts, 21 Furnace St., [Akron, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akron,_Ohio "Akron, Ohio")

Hynde opened the VegiTerranean, a [vegan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegan "Vegan") restaurant, in the Northside Lofts, Akron, Ohio[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-thevegiterranean/20110228093036-89) in November 2007. The restaurant served [fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusion_food "Fusion food") Italian-Mediterranean food[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-90) by head chef James Scot Jones. Before the restaurant's opening on September 15, 2007, Hynde performed three songs at the restaurant with [Adam Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Seymour_(musician) "Adam Seymour (musician)"), a former lead guitarist of the Pretenders. The restaurant was voted among the top five vegan restaurants in the U.S. It closed on October 2, 2011, owing to the economic climate, according to Hynde.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrissie_Hynde#cite_note-91)
