Throughout the next six decades, John cemented his status as a [cultural icon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_icon "Cultural icon") with [32 studio albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John_albums_discography "Elton John albums discography"), including _[Honky Château](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky\_Ch%C3%A2teau "Honky Château")_ (1972), _[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Yellow\_Brick\_Road "Goodbye Yellow Brick Road")_ (1973), _[Rock of the Westies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_of\_the\_Westies "Rock of the Westies")_ (1975), _[Sleeping with the Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeping\_with\_the\_Past "Sleeping with the Past")_ (1989), _[The One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_One\_(Elton\_John\_album) "The One (Elton John album)")_ (1992), _[Songs from the West Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songs\_from\_the\_West\_Coast "Songs from the West Coast")_ (2001), _[The Diving Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Diving\_Board "The Diving Board")_ (2013) and _[The Lockdown Sessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lockdown\_Sessions\_(Elton\_John\_album) "The Lockdown Sessions (Elton John album)")_ (2021). He has also had success in musical films and theatre, composing music for _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_ (1994), _[Aida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aida\_(musical) "Aida (musical)")_ (2000) and _[Billy Elliot the Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Elliot\_the\_Musical "Billy Elliot the Musical")_ (2005). John's final tour, [Farewell Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Yellow_Brick_Road "Farewell Yellow Brick Road") (2018–2023), became the [highest-grossing tour ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_concert_tours "List of highest-grossing concert tours") at the time. His life and career were dramatised in the 2019 biographical film _[Rocketman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocketman\_(film) "Rocketman (film)")_.

John is an [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS") charity fundraiser and has been involved in the fight against AIDS since the late 1980s.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-5) In 1992 he established the [Elton John AIDS Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John_AIDS_Foundation "Elton John AIDS Foundation"), which has raised over £300 million since its inception, and a year later he began hosting [his annual AIDS Foundation Academy Awards Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John_AIDS_Foundation_Academy_Award_Party "Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Award Party"), which has since become one of the biggest high-profile Oscars parties in the [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") film industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Foundation-6) John was the chairman and director of [Watford Football Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watford_Football_Club "Watford Football Club") from 1976 to 1987, and again from 1997 to 2002, and is an honorary life president of the club.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-8) From the late 1970s to the late 1980s, John developed a severe addiction to drugs and alcohol, but has been clean and sober since 1990.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-9) In 2005 he entered a [civil partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_partnership_in_the_United_Kingdom "Civil partnership in the United Kingdom") with his long-term partner, the Canadian filmmaker [David Furnish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Furnish "David Furnish"). They married in 2014, when [same-sex marriage was legalised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Same-sex_marriage_in_the_United_Kingdom "Same-sex marriage in the United Kingdom") in England and Wales.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-10)

John has had nine number-one singles on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") and the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), as well as seven consecutive number-one albums on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). He is the most successful solo artist in the history of the US [_Billboard_ charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts "Billboard charts"), and was the first solo artist with UK top 10 singles across six decades. His tribute single to [Diana, Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Diana, Princess of Wales"), "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")", a rewritten version of [his 1974 single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind "Candle in the Wind"), is the [best-selling chart single of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles "List of best-selling singles").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-AFP-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Guinness-12) John was inducted into the [Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Songwriters Hall of Fame") and the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame"), and is a fellow of [The Ivors Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ivors_Academy "The Ivors Academy"). He was appointed [Knight Bachelor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_Bachelor "Knight Bachelor") for services to music and charity in 1998 and was appointed a member of the [Order of the Companions of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Companions_of_Honour "Order of the Companions of Honour") in 2020. _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked him among the [greatest artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_100_Greatest_Artists_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Artists of All Time"), [greatest singers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_200_Greatest_Singers_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 200 Greatest Singers of All Time") and [greatest songwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone's_100_Greatest_Songwriters_of_All_Time "Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Songwriters of All Time") of all time.

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Reginald Kenneth Dwight was born on 25 March 1947 in [Pinner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinner "Pinner"), [Middlesex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesex "Middlesex") (now part of the [London Borough of Harrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Borough_of_Harrow "London Borough of Harrow")), the eldest child of Stanley Dwight (1925–1991) and only child of Sheila Eileen (née Harris; 1925–2017), who had married in 1945.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Telegraph-detective-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-15) He was raised in a [council house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_house "Council house") in Pinner where his maternal grandparents lived.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-55Pinner-16) When he was six, the family moved to a nearby semi-detached house.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-55Pinner-16)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Telegraph-detective-13)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-17) He was educated at Pinner Wood Junior School, Reddiford School and [Pinner County Grammar School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinner_County_Grammar_School "Pinner County Grammar School"), until he was 17, when he left just before his [A-Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-Level "A-Level") examinations to pursue a career in music.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Norman-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-VisualDoc-20)

When John began to consider a career in music seriously, his father, who served in the [Royal Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force "Royal Air Force"), tried to steer him toward a more conventional career, such as banking.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-21)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Norman-18) John has said that his wild stage costumes and performances were his way of letting go after a restrictive childhood.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-VisualDoc-20) Both his parents were musically inclined, his father having been a trumpet player with the Bob Millar Band, a semi-professional big band that played at military dances.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-VisualDoc-20) The Dwights were keen record buyers, exposing John to the popular singers and musicians of the day. John started playing his grandmother's piano as a young boy,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-22) and within a year his mother heard him picking out [Émile Waldteufel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%89mile_Waldteufel "Émile Waldteufel")'s "The [Skater's Waltz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skater's_Waltz "Skater's Waltz")" by ear.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Norman-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) After performing at parties and family gatherings, at age seven, he began formal piano lessons. He showed musical aptitude at school, including the ability to compose melodies, and garnered attention for playing like [Jerry Lee Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lee_Lewis "Jerry Lee Lewis") at school functions. At age 11, he won a junior scholarship to the [Royal Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academy_of_Music "Royal Academy of Music"). According to one of his instructors, John promptly played back, like a "gramophone record", a four-page piece by [George Frideric Handel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Frideric_Handel "George Frideric Handel") after hearing it for the first time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Royal_Academy_of_Music.jpg/250px-Royal_Academy_of_Music.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Royal_Academy_of_Music.jpg)

Elton John, known then as Reg Dwight, studied at the [Royal Academy of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academy_of_Music "Royal Academy of Music") in London for five years.

For the next five years, John attended Saturday classes at the academy in Central London, and he has said he enjoyed playing [Frédéric Chopin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Chopin "Frédéric Chopin") and [Johann Sebastian Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach "Johann Sebastian Bach") and singing in the choir during Saturday classes, but that he was not otherwise a diligent classical student.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) "I kind of resented going to the Academy," he said. "I was one of those children who could just about get away without practising and still pass, scrape through the grades."[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) He has said that he would sometimes skip classes and ride around on the [London Underground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Underground "London Underground").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) Several instructors have attested that he was a "model student", and during the last few years he took lessons from a private tutor in addition to his classes at the academy.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) He left the academy before taking the final exams.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-bbc60-23)

John's mother, though strict with her son, was more outgoing than her husband, and something of a free spirit. With Stanley Dwight uninterested in his son and often absent, John was raised primarily by his mother and maternal grandmother. When his father was home, the Dwights had vehement arguments that greatly distressed John.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) When he was 14, they divorced. His mother then married a local painter, Fred Farebrother, a caring and supportive stepfather whom John affectionately called "Derf", "Fred" backward.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) They moved into flat No.3A in an eight-unit apartment building called Frome Court, not far from both previous homes. There John wrote the songs that launched his career as a rock star. He lived there until he had four albums, simultaneously, in the American Top 40.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-24)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1962–1969: Pub pianist to staff songwriter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1962–1969: Pub pianist to staff songwriter")]

See also: [Bluesology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluesology "Bluesology")

At age 15, with his mother's and stepfather's help, John was hired as a pianist at a nearby pub, the Northwood Hills Hotel, playing Thursday to Sunday nights.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-26) Known simply as "Reggie", he played a range of popular standards, including songs by [Jim Reeves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Reeves "Jim Reeves") and [Ray Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Charles "Ray Charles"), as well as his own songs.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Costello_interview-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-p70-28) A stint with a short-lived group called the Corvettes rounded out his time.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rosenthal-19) Although normal-sighted as a teenager, John began wearing horn-rimmed glasses to imitate [Buddy Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddy_Holly "Buddy Holly").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-30)

In 1962, John and some friends formed a band named [Bluesology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluesology "Bluesology"). By day, he ran errands for a music publishing company; he divided his nights between solo gigs at a London hotel bar and working with Bluesology. By the mid-1960s, Bluesology were backing touring American [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music") and R&B musicians such as [the Isley Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Isley_Brothers "The Isley Brothers"), [Major Lance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Lance "Major Lance") and [Patti LaBelle and the Bluebelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patti_LaBelle_and_the_Bluebelles "Patti LaBelle and the Bluebelles"). In 1966 the band became [Long John Baldry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_John_Baldry "Long John Baldry")'s supporting band and played 16 times at the [Marquee Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquee_Club "Marquee Club").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-31)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/EltonJohnPiano.jpg/250px-EltonJohnPiano.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EltonJohnPiano.jpg)

The 1910 piano on which John composed his first five albums

In 1967 John answered an advertisement in the British music paper _[New Musical Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Musical\_Express "New Musical Express")_, placed by [Ray Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Williams_(producer) "Ray Williams (producer)"), then the [A&R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A&R "A&R") manager for [Liberty Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Records "Liberty Records").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-bilb-32) At their first meeting, Williams gave John an unopened envelope of lyrics written by [Bernie Taupin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Taupin "Bernie Taupin"), who had answered the same ad.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-33) John wrote music for the lyrics and then sent it to Taupin, which began their decades-long partnership that still continues[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit). When the two first met in 1967, they recorded the first John/Taupin song, "Scarecrow". Six months later, John began going by the name Elton John in homage to two members of Bluesology: the saxophonist [Elton Dean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_Dean "Elton Dean") and the vocalist [Long John Baldry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_John_Baldry "Long John Baldry").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Costello_interview-27) He legally [changed his name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_change#United_Kingdom "Name change") to Elton Hercules John on 7 January 1972.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-34) "Hercules" came from the name of a horse in British sitcom _[Steptoe and Son](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steptoe\_and\_Son "Steptoe and Son")_, of which John was a big fan.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-35)

The team of John and Taupin joined [Dick James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_James "Dick James")'s [DJM Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJM_Records "DJM Records") as staff songwriters in 1968, and over the next two years wrote material for various artists, among them [Roger Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Cook_(songwriter) "Roger Cook (songwriter)") and [Lulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lulu_(singer) "Lulu (singer)").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Vinita-36) Taupin would write a batch of lyrics in under an hour and give it to John, who would write music for each of them in half an hour, disposing of the lyrics if he could not come up with anything quickly.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Vinita-36) For two years they wrote [easy-listening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easy-listening "Easy-listening") tunes for James to peddle to singers. Their early output included a contender for the UK entry for the [Eurovision Song Contest 1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_1969 "Eurovision Song Contest 1969"), for Lulu, called "I Can't Go On (Living Without You)". It [came sixth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_1969 "United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest 1969") of six songs. In 1969, John provided piano for [Roger Hodgson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Hodgson "Roger Hodgson") on his first released single, "Mr. Boyd" by Argosy, a quartet that was completed by [Caleb Quaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb_Quaye "Caleb Quaye") and [Nigel Olsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Olsson "Nigel Olsson").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-38)

### 1969–1973: _Empty Sky_ to _Goodbye Yellow Brick Road_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1969–1973: Empty Sky to Goodbye Yellow Brick Road")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Popzanger_Elton_John_in_Nederland_Elton_John_%2C_kop%2C_Bestanddeelnr_924-2765_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Popzanger_Elton_John_in_Nederland_Elton_John_%2C_kop%2C_Bestanddeelnr_924-2765_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Popzanger_Elton_John_in_Nederland_Elton_John_,_kop,_Bestanddeelnr_924-2765_(cropped).jpg)

John in 1971

On the advice of music publisher Steve Brown, John and Taupin began writing more complex songs for John to record for DJM. The first was the single "[I've Been Loving You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I've_Been_Loving_You "I've Been Loving You")" (1968), produced by [Caleb Quaye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb_Quaye "Caleb Quaye"), Bluesology's former guitarist. In 1969, with Quaye, the drummer Roger Pope and the bassist Tony Murray, John recorded another single, "[Lady Samantha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Samantha "Lady Samantha")", and an album, _[Empty Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empty\_Sky "Empty Sky")_. For their follow-up album, _[Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton\_John\_(album) "Elton John (album)")_, John and Taupin enlisted [Gus Dudgeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_Dudgeon "Gus Dudgeon") as producer and [Paul Buckmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Buckmaster "Paul Buckmaster") as musical arranger.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)

_Elton John_ was released in April 1970 on DJM Records/[Pye Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pye_Records "Pye Records") in the UK and [Uni Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uni_Records "Uni Records") in the US, and established the formula for subsequent albums: gospel-chorded rockers and poignant ballads. The album's first single, "[Border Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border_Song "Border Song")", peaked at 92 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). The second, "[Your Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Your_Song "Your Song")", reached number seven in the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") and number eight in the US, becoming John's first hit single as a singer.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) The album soon became his first hit album, reaching number four on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") and number five on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-40)

Backed by the former [Spencer Davis Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Spencer_Davis_Group "The Spencer Davis Group")[rhythm section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_section "Rhythm section"), drummer [Nigel Olsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_Olsson "Nigel Olsson") and bassist [Dee Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dee_Murray "Dee Murray"), John's first American concert took place at the [Troubadour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubadour_(West_Hollywood,_California) "Troubadour (West Hollywood, California)") in Los Angeles, California, on 25 August 1970, and was a success.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-41) The concept album _[Tumbleweed Connection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumbleweed\_Connection "Tumbleweed Connection")_ was released in October 1970 and reached number two in the UK and number five in the US.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) The live album _[17-11-70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17-11-70 "17-11-70")_ (titled _11–17–70_ in the US) was recorded at a live show aired from A&R Studios on [WABC-FM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WABC-FM "WABC-FM") in New York City. Sales of the live album took a blow in the US when an east-coast [bootlegger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bootleg_recording "Bootleg recording") released the performance several weeks before the official album, including all 60 minutes of the aircast, not just the 40 minutes selected by Dick James Music.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-42)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Elton_John_Hamburg_1972_1603720004.jpg/250px-Elton_John_Hamburg_1972_1603720004.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_Hamburg_1972_1603720004.jpg)

John at the [Musikhalle Hamburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musikhalle_Hamburg "Musikhalle Hamburg"), in March 1972

John and Taupin wrote the soundtrack to the 1971 film _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends\_(1971\_film) "Friends (1971 film)")_ and the album _[Madman Across the Water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madman\_Across\_the\_Water "Madman Across the Water")_, which reached number eight in the US and included the hit songs "[Levon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levon_(song) "Levon (song)")" and the album's opening track, "[Tiny Dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiny_Dancer "Tiny Dancer")". In 1972 [Davey Johnstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_Johnstone "Davey Johnstone") joined the Elton John Band on guitar and backing vocals. Released in 1972, _[Honky Château](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky\_Ch%C3%A2teau "Honky Château")_ became John's first US number-one album, spending five weeks at the top of the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), and began a streak of seven consecutive US number-one albums.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-43) The album reached number two in the UK, and spawned the hit singles "[Rocket Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Man_(song) "Rocket Man (song)")" and "[Honky Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honky_Cat "Honky Cat")".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-44)

In 1972 John performed at the [Royal Variety Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Variety_Performance "Royal Variety Performance"), where he was upstaged by the dancing of [Larry Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Smith_(musician) "Larry Smith (musician)"), the drummer with the [Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonzo_Dog_Doo-Dah_Band "Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-45) Smith was invited to join John's second US tour; Smith later said: "I suggested adding in various other bizarre elements like me doing "[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'_in_the_Rain_(song) "Singin' in the Rain (song)")" as a song and dance act with Elton playing piano. Kubrick's _[Clockwork Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Clockwork\_Orange\_(film) "A Clockwork Orange (film)")_ film had recently featured that song. Plus I designed crazy, over-the-top costumes and giant stage sets – known as 'Legstravaganzas'. Elton loved all of it."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-46)

The pop album _[Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Shoot\_Me\_I'm\_Only\_the\_Piano\_Player "Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player")_ came out at the start of 1973 and reached number one in the UK, the US, and Australia, among other countries.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) The album produced the hits "[Crocodile Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocodile_Rock "Crocodile Rock")", his first US _Billboard_ Hot 100 number one, and "[Daniel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_(Elton_John_song) "Daniel (Elton John song)")", which reached number two in the US and number four in the UK.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-47) The album and "Crocodile Rock" were respectively the first album and single on the consolidated [MCA Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCA_Records "MCA Records") label in the US, replacing MCA's other labels, including Uni.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-48)

_[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye\_Yellow\_Brick\_Road "Goodbye Yellow Brick Road")_, a double-album released in October 1973, gained instant critical acclaim and topped the chart on both sides of the Atlantic, remaining at number one for two months.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Redbeard_GYBR_interview-49) It also temporarily established John as a [glam rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_rock "Glam rock") star. It contained the US number 1 "[Bennie and the Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bennie_and_the_Jets "Bennie and the Jets")", along with the hits "[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_Yellow_Brick_Road_(song) "Goodbye Yellow Brick Road (song)")", "[Candle in the Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind "Candle in the Wind")" and "[Saturday Night's Alright for Fighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night's_Alright_for_Fighting "Saturday Night's Alright for Fighting")", as well as live favourites "[Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funeral_for_a_Friend/Love_Lies_Bleeding "Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding")" and "[Harmony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony_(Elton_John_song) "Harmony (Elton John song)")".

### 1974–1980: The Rocket Record Company to _21 at 33_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1974–1980: The Rocket Record Company to 21 at 33")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/Elton_John.jpg/250px-Elton_John.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John.jpg)

John on the piano during a live performance in 1975

John formed his own record label, [The Rocket Record Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rocket_Record_Company "The Rocket Record Company") (distributed in the US by MCA and initially by Island in the UK), and signed acts to it—notably [Neil Sedaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Sedaka "Neil Sedaka") (John sang background vocals on Sedaka's "[Bad Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Blood_(Neil_Sedaka_song) "Bad Blood (Neil Sedaka song)")") and [Kiki Dee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiki_Dee "Kiki Dee"), in whom he took a personal interest. Rather than releasing his own records through The Rocket Record Company, John signed an US$8 million contract with MCA Records. Upon the signing of the deal in 1974, MCA reportedly secured a $25 million insurance policy on his life.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-50) In 1974 MCA released _[Elton John's Greatest Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton\_John's\_Greatest\_Hits "Elton John's Greatest Hits")_, a UK and US number one that is [certified Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#RIAA_Diamond_certifications "RIAA certification") by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA "RIAA") for US sales of 17 million copies.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-51)

In 1974 John collaborated with [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") on his cover of [the Beatles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beatles "The Beatles")' "[Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_in_the_Sky_with_Diamonds "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds")", the B-side of which was Lennon's "One Day at a Time". It was number 1 for two weeks in the US. In return, John was featured on "[Whatever Gets You Thru the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatever_Gets_You_Thru_the_Night "Whatever Gets You Thru the Night")" on Lennon's album _[Walls and Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walls\_and\_Bridges "Walls and Bridges")_. Later that year, in Lennon's last major live performance, the pair performed these two number-one hits, along with the Beatles' "[I Saw Her Standing There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Saw_Her_Standing_There "I Saw Her Standing There")", at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") in New York City. Lennon made the rare stage appearance with John and his band to keep the promise he had made that he would appear on stage with him if "Whatever Gets You Thru The Night" became a US number-one single.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-52)_[Caribou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribou\_(album) "Caribou (album)")_ was released in 1974, becoming John's third number one in the UK and topping the charts in the US, Canada and Australia.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-artists.letssingit.com-53) Reportedly recorded in two weeks between live appearances, it featured "[The Bitch Is Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bitch_Is_Back "The Bitch Is Back")" and "[Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Let_the_Sun_Go_Down_on_Me "Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me")".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-artists.letssingit.com-53) "[Step into Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step_into_Christmas "Step into Christmas")" was released as a stand-alone single in November 1973, and appears in the album's 1995 remastered reissue.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-54)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Elton_john_cher_show_1975.JPG/250px-Elton_john_cher_show_1975.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_john_cher_show_1975.JPG)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Elton_John%E2%80%99s_shoes_%284%29_%2823219556921%29.jpg/250px-Elton_John%E2%80%99s_shoes_%284%29_%2823219556921%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John%E2%80%99s_shoes_(4)_(23219556921).jpg)

Influenced by the [glam rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glam_rock "Glam rock") scene in the UK, John (pictured left on the _[Cher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher\_(TV\_series) "Cher (TV series)")_ show) often wore elaborate stage costumes, including platform boots (right).[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-55)

[Pete Townshend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Townshend "Pete Townshend") of [the Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Who "The Who") asked John to play the "Local Lad" in [the 1975 film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_(1975_film) "Tommy (1975 film)") of the [rock opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_opera "Rock opera")_[Tommy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy\_(The\_Who\_album) "Tommy (The Who album)")_, and to perform the song "[Pinball Wizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinball_Wizard "Pinball Wizard")". Drawing on [power chords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_chord "Power chord"), John's version was recorded and used in the movie. The song charted at number 7 in the UK.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) John, who had adopted a glam aesthetic on stage, would later state glam rock icon [Marc Bolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Bolan "Marc Bolan") "had a great effect on me."[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-56)

The 1975 autobiographical album _[Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain\_Fantastic\_and\_the\_Brown\_Dirt\_Cowboy "Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy")_ debuted at number one in the US, the [first album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200#Additional_milestones "Billboard 200") to do so, and stayed there for seven weeks.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-record-57) John revealed his previously ambiguous personality on the album, with Taupin's lyrics describing their early days as struggling songwriters and musicians in London. The lyrics and accompanying photo booklet are infused with a specific sense of place and time that is otherwise rare in his music. The hit single from this album, "[Someone Saved My Life Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_Saved_My_Life_Tonight "Someone Saved My Life Tonight")", captured an early turning point in John's life. The album's release signalled the end of the Elton John Band, as an unhappy and overworked John dismissed Olsson and Murray.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Hombach-58)

According to _[Circus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus\_(magazine) "Circus (magazine)")_, a spokesman for John's manager [John Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Reid_(music_manager) "John Reid (music manager)") said the decision was reached mutually via phone while John was in Australia promoting _Tommy_.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-raves-59) Davey Johnstone and Ray Cooper were retained, Quaye and Roger Pope returned, and the new bassist was Kenny Passarelli; this rhythm section provided a heavier backbeat. [James Newton Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Newton_Howard "James Newton Howard") joined to arrange in the studio and to play keyboards.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Elton_Band-60) In June 1975 John introduced the line-up at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)") in London.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Elton_Band-60)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/Elton_John_receiving_his_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg/250px-Elton_John_receiving_his_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_receiving_his_star_on_the_Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame.jpg)

John receiving his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1975

The rock-oriented _[Rock of the Westies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_of\_the\_Westies "Rock of the Westies")_ entered the US albums chart at number 1, as had _Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy_, a previously unattained feat.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-record-57) John's stage wardrobe now included ostrich feathers, $5,000 spectacles that spelled his name in lights, and costumes such as the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty"), [Donald Duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Duck "Donald Duck"), and [Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Amadeus_Mozart "Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-61) In 1975 he received a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-HWOF-62) The album features his fifth US number-one single, "[Island Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Girl "Island Girl")". To celebrate five years since he had first appeared at the venue, in 1975 John played a two-night, four-show stand at [the Troubadour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubadour_(Los_Angeles) "The Troubadour (Los Angeles)"). With seating limited to fewer than 500 attendees per show, tickets were distributed through a postcard lottery system, with each selected individual eligible to purchase two tickets. All attendees received a hardbound "yearbook" documenting the band's history. That year, he also played piano on [Kevin Ayers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Ayers "Kevin Ayers")'s _[Sweet Deceiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet\_Deceiver "Sweet Deceiver")_ and was among the first and few white artists to appear on the African-American television series _[Soul Train](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Train "Soul Train")_.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Redbeard_GYBR_interview-49)

On 9 August 1975 John was named the outstanding rock personality of the year at the first annual Rock Music Awards in Santa Monica, California, US.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-63) After a botched suicide attempt the day before, John performed at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") in Los Angeles for two nights in a row on October 25 and 26. These shows are considered among the most successful of his career, and featured his most enduring stage costume; a sequined [Dodger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Dodgers "Los Angeles Dodgers") baseball uniform designed by [Bob Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Mackie "Bob Mackie").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Elton_John_at_Dodger_Stadium-64)

In May 1976 the live album _[Here and There](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_and\_There\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Here and There (Elton John album)")_ was released, followed in October by the album _[Blue Moves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Moves "Blue Moves")_, which contained the single "[Sorry Seems to Be the Hardest Word](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorry_Seems_to_Be_the_Hardest_Word "Sorry Seems to Be the Hardest Word")". His biggest success in 1976 was "[Don't Go Breaking My Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_Breaking_My_Heart "Don't Go Breaking My Heart")", a duet with Kiki Dee that topped a number of charts, including the UK, the US, Australia, France and Canada.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_Charts-65)

In addition to being the most commercially successful period of John's career, the years 1970 to 1976 are also widely regarded as his critical peak. Between 1972 and 1975, he achieved seven consecutive number-one albums in the United States, a feat that had not been accomplished prior to that time.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Redbeard_GYBR_interview-49) All six of his albums to make _Rolling Stone_'s 2003 list of "[The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_500_Greatest_Albums_of_All_Time "The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time")" are from this period, with _Goodbye Yellow Brick Road_ ranked highest at number 91.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-66) Between 1972 and 1976 he also had six singles reach number one on the _Billboard_ Hot 100.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_charts-67)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Elton_John_1.jpg/250px-Elton_John_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_1.jpg)

John performing live in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin") with [Ray Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Cooper "Ray Cooper") in 1979

In November 1977, John announced he was retiring from performing; Taupin began collaborating with others. Now producing only one album a year, John issued _[A Single Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Single\_Man\_(album) "A Single Man (album)")_ in 1978, with a new lyricist, [Gary Osborne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Osborne "Gary Osborne"); the album produced no singles that made the top 20 in the US, but the two singles from the album released in the UK, "[Part-Time Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Part-Time_Love "Part-Time Love")" and "[Song for Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_for_Guy "Song for Guy")", both made the top 20 there, with the latter reaching the top 5.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) In 1979, accompanied by [Ray Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Cooper "Ray Cooper"), John became one of the first Western artists to tour the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and Israel.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-69) John returned to the US top ten with "[Mama Can't Buy You Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama_Can't_Buy_You_Love "Mama Can't Buy You Love")" (number 9), a song MCA rejected in 1977, recorded with the American soul producer [Thom Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thom_Bell "Thom Bell").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-70) John said Bell was the first person to give him voice lessons and encouraged him to sing in a lower register.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-71)

A [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco")-influenced album, _[Victim of Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victim\_of\_Love\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Victim of Love (Elton John album)")_, was poorly received. In 1979 John and Taupin reunited, although they did not collaborate on a full album until 1983's _[Too Low For Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too\_Low\_For\_Zero "Too Low For Zero")_. _[21 at 33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_at\_33 "21 at 33")_, released in 1980, was a significant career boost, aided by his biggest hit in four years, "[Little Jeannie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Jeannie "Little Jeannie")" (number 3 US), with the lyrics by Gary Osborne.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-72) In May 1979 John played eight [concerts in the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music_and_the_fall_of_communism "Rock music and the fall of communism"); four dates in Leningrad (now [Saint Petersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg")) and four in Moscow.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-73) At the same time, John collaborated with the French couple [France Gall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Gall "France Gall") and [Michel Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Berger "Michel Berger") on the songs "Donner pour donner" and "Les Aveux", released together in 1980 as a single.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-74)

### 1981–1989: _The Fox_ to _Sleeping with the Past_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1981–1989: The Fox to Sleeping with the Past")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Elton_John_in_1980s.jpg/250px-Elton_John_in_1980s.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_in_1980s.jpg)

John performing in 1986

John's 1981 album _[The Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fox\_(Elton\_John\_album) "The Fox (Elton John album)")_ was recorded during the same sessions as _[21 at 33](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21\_at\_33 "21 at 33")_ and included collaborations with [Tom Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Robinson "Tom Robinson") and [Judie Tzuke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judie_Tzuke "Judie Tzuke"). On 13 September 1980, with Olsson and Murray back in the Elton John Band, and joined by [Richie Zito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richie_Zito "Richie Zito") on lead guitar, [Tim Renwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Renwick "Tim Renwick") on rhythm guitar, and [James Newton Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Newton_Howard "James Newton Howard") on keyboards, John performed a free concert to an estimated 400,000 fans on The Great Lawn in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park") in New York City.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-75) He played part of the set dressed as [Donald Duck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Duck "Donald Duck").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-76) The album _[Jump Up!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump\_Up!\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Jump Up! (Elton John album)")_ was released in 1982, the biggest hit from which was "[Blue Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Eyes_(Elton_John_song) "Blue Eyes (Elton John song)")".[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-77) Also on that album is “[Empty Garden (Hey Hey Johnny)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empty_Garden_(Hey_Hey_Johnny) "Empty Garden (Hey Hey Johnny)")”, written in the wake of [John Lennon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon")’s [1980 murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_John_Lennon "Murder of John Lennon").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-78)

With the original band members Johnstone, Murray and Olsson together again, John returned to the charts with the 1983 album _[Too Low for Zero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too\_Low\_for\_Zero "Too Low for Zero")_, which included the singles "[I'm Still Standing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Standing "I'm Still Standing")" (No. 4 UK) and "[I Guess That's Why They Call It the Blues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Guess_That's_Why_They_Call_It_the_Blues "I Guess That's Why They Call It the Blues")", the latter of which featured [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") on harmonica and reached number four in the US and number five in the UK.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_Charts-65) In October 1983 John caused controversy when he broke the United Nations' cultural boycott on [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid")-era South Africa by performing at [Sun City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_City,_North_West "Sun City, North West").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-79) He married his close friend and sound engineer, Renate Blauel, on Valentine's Day 1984; the marriage lasted three years.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-80) In 1984 he released _[Breaking Hearts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaking\_Hearts "Breaking Hearts")_, which featured the song "[Sad Songs (Say So Much)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sad_Songs_(Say_So_Much) "Sad Songs (Say So Much)")", a number five hit in the US and number seven in the UK.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Elton_John_costume.jpg/250px-Elton_John_costume.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_costume.jpg)

John costume from the 1986 [Tour de Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_De_Force_(tour) "Tour De Force (tour)") Australian concerts, on display in the [Hard Rock Cafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Cafe "Hard Rock Cafe"), London

In 1985 John was one of the many performers at [Live Aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Aid "Live Aid"), held at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-p_fifty_seven-81) John performed "Bennie and the Jets" and "Rocket Man" at Live Aid before performing with [Kiki Dee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiki_Dee "Kiki Dee") for the first time since 1982. He concluded by introducing [George Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Michael "George Michael") (then of [Wham!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wham! "Wham!")) for "Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-p_fifty_seven-81) John also recorded material with [Millie Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millie_Jackson "Millie Jackson") in 1985. Towards the end of the year, John released "[Nikita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_(song) "Nikita (song)")" from the album _[Ice on Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice\_on\_Fire "Ice on Fire")_, which had a music video directed by [Ken Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Russell "Ken Russell"). The song reached number three in the UK and number seven in the US.

John's highest-charting single of the decade was a collaboration with [Dionne Warwick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dionne_Warwick "Dionne Warwick"), [Gladys Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladys_Knight "Gladys Knight") and Stevie Wonder called "[That's What Friends Are For](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's_What_Friends_Are_For "That's What Friends Are For")". It reached number one in the US at the beginning of 1986; credited as Dionne and Friends, the song raised funds for [HIV/AIDS research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_research "HIV/AIDS research").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_Charts-65) In the same year, a live orchestral version of "Candle in the Wind" reached number six in the US. He also played piano on two tracks on the [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band [Saxon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxon_(band) "Saxon (band)")'s album _[Rock the Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock\_the\_Nations "Rock the Nations")_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-82)

In 1988 John performed five sold-out shows at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") in New York City, giving him 26 for his career.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-83) Netting over $20 million, 2,000 items of John's memorabilia were auctioned off at [Sotheby's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sotheby's "Sotheby's") in London.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-84) He also released "[I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Don't_Wanna_Go_On_with_You_Like_That "I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That")" from the album _[Reg Strikes Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reg\_Strikes\_Back "Reg Strikes Back")_, the single reaching number two in the US in 1988.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_Charts-65) His albums continued to sell, but of those released in the latter half of the 1980s, only _Reg Strikes Back_ (number 16, 1988) placed in the top 20 in the US.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Billboard_Charts-65)

### 1990–1999: "Sacrifice" to _Aida_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1990–1999: \"Sacrifice\" to Aida")]

In 1990 John achieved his first solo UK number one hit single, with "[Sacrifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice_(Elton_John_song) "Sacrifice (Elton John song)")" (coupled with "[Healing Hands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healing_Hands_(Elton_John_song) "Healing Hands (Elton John song)")") from the previous year's album _[Sleeping with the Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeping\_with\_the\_Past "Sleeping with the Past")_; it stayed at the top spot for five weeks.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-85) The following year, "Basque" won the [Grammy for Best Instrumental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Instrumental_Composition "Grammy Award for Best Instrumental Composition"), and a guest concert appearance at [Wembley Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Arena "Wembley Arena") John made on [George Michael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Michael "George Michael")'s cover of "[Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Let_the_Sun_Go_Down_on_Me "Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me")" was released as a single and topped the charts in both the UK and the US.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-86) At the [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_BRIT_Awards_ceremonies#1991 "List of BRIT Awards ceremonies")[Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards") in London, John won Best British Male.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-87)

In 1992 John released the US number 8 album _[The One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_One\_(Elton\_John\_album) "The One (Elton John album)")_, featuring the hit song "[The One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_One_(Elton_John_song) "The One (Elton John song)")".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-88) It was his first album recorded entirely sober. As John recalled in 2020, "I was used to making records under the haze of alcohol or drugs, and here I was, 100% sober, so it was tough. But I managed to come up with a good song, which was the title of the record."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-89) He also released "[Runaway Train](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_Train_(Elton_John_and_Eric_Clapton_song) "Runaway Train (Elton John and Eric Clapton song)")", a duet he recorded with his longtime friend [Eric Clapton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Clapton "Eric Clapton"), with whom he played on [Clapton's World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clapton's_World_Tour "Clapton's World Tour").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-90) John and Taupin then signed a music publishing deal with [Warner/Chappell Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner/Chappell_Music "Warner/Chappell Music") for an estimated $39 million over 12 years, including the largest cash advance in music publishing history.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-91)

In April 1992 John appeared at the [Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury_Tribute_Concert "Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert") at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)"), performing "[The Show Must Go On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Show_Must_Go_On_(Queen_song) "The Show Must Go On (Queen song)")" with the remaining members of [Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_(band) "Queen (band)"), and "[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian_Rhapsody "Bohemian Rhapsody")" with [Axl Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axl_Rose "Axl Rose") of [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses") and Queen's remaining members.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-92) In September John performed "The One" at the [1992 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "1992 MTV Video Music Awards") and closed the ceremony performing "[November Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_Rain "November Rain")" with Guns N' Roses.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-93) In 1993 he released _[Duets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duets\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Duets (Elton John album)")_, which featured collaborations with 15 artists, including [Tammy Wynette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammy_Wynette "Tammy Wynette") and [RuPaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RuPaul "RuPaul"). This included a new collaboration with Kiki Dee, "[True Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_Love_(Cole_Porter_song) "True Love (Cole Porter song)")", which reached the Top 10 of the UK charts.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-94) In the same year, _The Bunbury Tails_, a multi-artist charity album, was released, which was the soundtrack to the British [animated television series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animated_series "Animated series") of the same name. "Up The Revolution" was John's track, alongside contributions from [George Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Harrison "George Harrison"), the [Bee Gees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bee_Gees "Bee Gees") and Eric Clapton. The album was issued briefly, and only in the UK.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-95)

> "For myself as well as for many others no one has been there more for inspiration than Elton John. When we talk of great rock duos like [Jimmy Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Page "Jimmy Page") and [Robert Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Plant "Robert Plant"), [John (Lennon)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lennon "John Lennon") and [Paul (McCartney)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney"), [Mick (Jagger)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Jagger "Mick Jagger") and [Keith (Richards)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Richards "Keith Richards"), I like to think of Elton John and Bernie Taupin. Also tonight I think that Elton should be honoured for his great work and contribution in the fight against AIDS. And also his bravery in exposing all the triumphs and tragedies of his personal life."

—[Axl Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axl_Rose "Axl Rose") speech inducting Elton John into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-96)

Along with [Tim Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Rice "Tim Rice"), John wrote the songs for the 1994 [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") animated film _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_. At the [67th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards "67th Academy Awards"), three of the five nominees for the [Academy Award for Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song") were from [_The Lion King_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_King_(1994_soundtrack) "The Lion King (1994 soundtrack)"). John won the award for "[Can You Feel the Love Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can_You_Feel_the_Love_Tonight "Can You Feel the Love Tonight")".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-BILL-97) Both that and "[Circle of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_of_Life "Circle of Life")" became hits.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-99) "Can You Feel the Love Tonight" also won the [Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Male_Pop_Vocal_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance") at the [37th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/37th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "37th Annual Grammy Awards").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-100) The soundtrack for _The Lion King_ remained at the top of the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") for nine weeks. On 10 November 1999, the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA "RIAA") certified _The Lion King_ "[Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamond_record "Diamond record")" for selling 15 million copies.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-ELT-101)

In 1994, John was inducted into the [Rock and Roll Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_and_Roll_Hall_of_Fame "Rock and Roll Hall of Fame") by [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses")' frontman [Axl Rose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axl_Rose "Axl Rose").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Rock_Hall-102) In 1995 he released the album _[Made in England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Made\_in\_England\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Made in England (Elton John album)")_ (number 3). [The title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Made_in_England_(song) "Made in England (song)") is an autobiographical recounting of parts of his life. The album also featured the single "[Believe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believe_(Elton_John_song) "Believe (Elton John song)")".[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-103) John performed "Believe" at the [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_BRIT_Awards_ceremonies#1995 "List of BRIT Awards ceremonies")[Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards "Brit Awards") and won the Outstanding Contribution to Music prize.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-104) In September 1995, he appeared as Angel Rick on the original studio album of [Randy Newman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman "Randy Newman")'s musical [_Faust_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Newman's_Faust "Randy Newman's Faust").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-105)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg/250px-Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_with_Luciano_Pavarotti_in_Modena_1996.jpg)

John with [Luciano Pavarotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti "Luciano Pavarotti") in Modena, 1996

A duet with [Luciano Pavarotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luciano_Pavarotti "Luciano Pavarotti"), "[Live Like Horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Like_Horses "Live Like Horses")", reached number nine in the UK in December 1996.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Charts-39) A compilation album, _[Love Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Songs\_(Elton\_John\_album) "Love Songs (Elton John album)")_, was released in 1996.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-106) Early in 1997, John held a 50th birthday party, costumed as [Louis XIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV "Louis XIV"), with 500 friends. He performed with the surviving members of Queen in Paris at the opening night (17 January 1997) of _Le Presbytère N'a Rien Perdu De Son Charme Ni Le Jardin De Son Éclat_, a work by the French ballet dancer [Maurice Béjart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_B%C3%A9jart "Maurice Béjart") that draws upon the AIDS crisis and the deaths of [Freddie Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mercury "Freddie Mercury") and the company's principal dancer, [Jorge Donn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Donn "Jorge Donn"). Later in 1997, two close friends died: the designer [Gianni Versace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Versace "Gianni Versace") was murdered on 15 July, and [Diana, Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Diana, Princess of Wales"), died in a [Paris car crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_of_Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Death of Diana, Princess of Wales") on 31 August.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-107)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Westminster_Abbey_Interior_MOD_45152595.jpg/250px-Westminster_Abbey_Interior_MOD_45152595.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Westminster_Abbey_Interior_MOD_45152595.jpg)

Interior of [Westminster Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_Abbey "Westminster Abbey") where John performed "Candle in the Wind 1997" live for the only time at [Princess Diana's funeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funeral_of_Diana,_Princess_of_Wales "Funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales")

In early September John asked Taupin to revise the lyrics of their 1973 song "Candle in the Wind" to honour Diana, and Taupin agreed.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-108) On 6 September 1997 John performed "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")" live for the only time at [Diana's funeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana's_funeral "Diana's funeral") in [Westminster Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westminster_Abbey "Westminster Abbey").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Candle_live-110) The song became the fastest- and biggest-selling single of all time, eventually selling over 33 million copies globally.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-ELT-101)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-GRAM-111) The [best-selling single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles_in_the_United_Kingdom "List of best-selling singles in the United Kingdom") in UK chart history,[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-112) and the best-selling single in _Billboard_ history, it is the first single [certified Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") in the US where it sold over 11 million copies.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-ELT-101)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-113) The 2009 _[Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness\_World\_Records "Guinness World Records")_ states it is "the biggest-selling single since UK and US singles charts began in the 1950s, having accumulated worldwide sales of 33 million copies".[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Guinness-12) The song's proceeds of approximately £55 million were donated to Diana's charities via the [Diana, Princess of Wales Memorial Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana,_Princess_of_Wales_Memorial_Fund "Diana, Princess of Wales Memorial Fund"). It won the [Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Male_Pop_Vocal_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance") at the [40th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "40th Annual Grammy Awards") in 1998.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-GRAM-111) The song "[Something About the Way You Look Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_About_the_Way_You_Look_Tonight "Something About the Way You Look Tonight")" was released as a [double A-side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_A-side "Double A-side").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-Candle_live-110)

On 15 September 1997 John appeared at the _[Music for Montserrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_for\_Montserrat "Music for Montserrat")_ charity concert at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall") in London, performing three songs solo ("Your Song", "Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me" and "Live Like Horses") before finishing with "[Hey Jude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hey_Jude "Hey Jude")" alongside [Paul McCartney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney"), Eric Clapton, [Phil Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phil_Collins "Phil Collins"), [Mark Knopfler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Knopfler "Mark Knopfler") and [Sting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sting_(musician) "Sting (musician)").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-114) Two months later he performed on the BBC's [Children in Need](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_in_Need "Children in Need") charity single "[Perfect Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_Day_97 "Perfect Day 97")", which reached number one in the UK.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-115) John appeared as himself in the [Spice Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice_Girls "Spice Girls") film _[Spice World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spice\_World\_(film) "Spice World (film)")_, released in December 1997.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-116)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/President_Bill_Clinton_and_Prime_Minister_Tony_Blair_are_joined_on_stage_by_Elton_John_and_Stevie_Wonder.jpg/330px-President_Bill_Clinton_and_Prime_Minister_Tony_Blair_are_joined_on_stage_by_Elton_John_and_Stevie_Wonder.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Bill_Clinton_and_Prime_Minister_Tony_Blair_are_joined_on_stage_by_Elton_John_and_Stevie_Wonder.jpg)

John (second from left) alongside British Prime Minister [Tony Blair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Blair "Tony Blair") (left), the singer-songwriter [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder") and US President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in Washington, D.C., February 1998

[_The Lion King_ musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lion_King_(musical) "The Lion King (musical)") debuted on Broadway in 1997 and the [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") theatre in 1999. In 2014 it had grossed over $6 billion and became the top-earning title in box-office history for both stage productions and films, surpassing the record previously held by [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber")'s 1986 musical _[The Phantom of the Opera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Opera\_(1986\_musical) "The Phantom of the Opera (1986 musical)")_.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-117) In addition to _The Lion King_, John composed music for Disney's musical production _[Aida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aida\_(musical) "Aida (musical)")_ in 1999 with the lyricist [Tim Rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Rice "Tim Rice"), for which they received the [Tony Award for Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Tony Award for Best Original Score") at the [54th Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Tony_Awards "54th Tony Awards"),[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-118) and the [Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Musical_Show_Album "Grammy Award for Best Musical Show Album") at the [43rd Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/43rd_Annual_Grammy_Awards "43rd Annual Grammy Awards").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-119)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-bbc60-23)

The musical premiered at the Alliance Theatre in Atlanta, Georgia, US, before moving to Chicago, Illinois, and subsequently opening on Broadway in New York City. John released a live compilation album, _[Elton John One Night Only – The Greatest Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton\_John\_One\_Night\_Only\_%E2%80%93\_The\_Greatest\_Hits "Elton John One Night Only – The Greatest Hits")_, featuring songs from his show at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") in New York City that same year. A concept album of songs from the musical _Aida_, _[Elton John and Tim Rice's Aida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton\_John\_and\_Tim\_Rice's\_Aida "Elton John and Tim Rice's Aida")_, was also released and featured the John duets "[Written in the Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Written_in_the_Stars_(Elton_John_and_LeAnn_Rimes_song) "Written in the Stars (Elton John and LeAnn Rimes song)")" with [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes"), and "I Know the Truth" with [Janet Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Jackson "Janet Jackson").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-120)

### 2000–2009: _Billy Elliot the Musical_ and 60th birthday

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elton_John&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2000–2009: Billy Elliot the Musical and 60th birthday")]

By this time, John disliked appearing in his own music videos; the video for "[This Train Don't Stop There Anymore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Train_Don't_Stop_There_Anymore "This Train Don't Stop There Anymore")" featured [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake") portraying a young John, and the video for "[I Want Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Want_Love "I Want Love")" featured [Robert Downey Jr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Downey_Jr "Robert Downey Jr") lip-syncing the song.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-121) At the [2001 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Grammy_Awards "2001 Grammy Awards"), John performed "[Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_(song) "Stan (song)")" with [Eminem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eminem "Eminem").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-122) One month after the [11 September attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11_September_attacks "11 September attacks"), John appeared at [the Concert for New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Concert_for_New_York_City "The Concert for New York City"), performing "I Want Love" as well as "Your Song" as a duet with [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-123) In August 2003 John's fifth UK number-one single, "[Are You Ready for Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Are_You_Ready_for_Love "Are You Ready for Love")", topped the charts.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-124)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/90/Routemaster_bus_%281139836654%29.jpg/250px-Routemaster_bus_%281139836654%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Routemaster_bus_(1139836654).jpg)

Advertisement for John's West End musical _[Billy Elliot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Elliot\_the\_Musical "Billy Elliot the Musical")_ on a [Routemaster bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AEC_Routemaster "AEC Routemaster") in London, 2007

Returning to musical theatre, John composed music for a [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") theatre production of _[Billy Elliot the Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Elliot\_the\_Musical "Billy Elliot the Musical")_ in 2005 with playwright [Lee Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Hall_(playwright) "Lee Hall (playwright)"). John had been moved to write the musical after seeing the 2000 British coming-of-age film _[Billy Elliot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy\_Elliot "Billy Elliot")_, saying of the titular character, "he's like me".[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-125) Opening to strong reviews, the show won four [Laurence Olivier Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier_Awards "Laurence Olivier Awards"), including [Best New Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier_Award_for_Best_New_Musical "Laurence Olivier Award for Best New Musical"). The [12th-longest-running musical in West End history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_the_longest-running_West_End_shows "List of the longest-running West End shows"), the London production, which featured [Tom Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Holland "Tom Holland") as Billy for two years, ran through April 2016, with 4,566 performances.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John#cite_note-auto-126)
